h1: Is Les Mills Worth It in NZ? (2026 Review)
focus_keyword: is les mills worth it nz
intro: Les Mills is NZ's most established premium gym brand, but it isn't the cheapest. This honest 2026 review weighs the price against the classes, facilities and atmosphere — and who's better off with a budget chain instead.
h2_outline: Les Mills Pricing in 2026 — What You Actually Pay
What You Get for the Money
Who Should Choose Les Mills (and Who Shouldn't)

sections.heading: Les Mills Pricing in 2026 — What You Actually Pay
sections.body: Les Mills memberships start from around $17.99/week with a 3-month minimum term and a joining fee that's often waived in promotions. Under-23s typically get about 20% off. It sits at the premium end of the NZ market.

sections.heading: What You Get for the Money
sections.body: You're paying for large, well-equipped clubs, pools and saunas at many locations, and the widest group fitness timetable in NZ — BodyPump, RPM, BodyCombat, Grit and more, all created in-house.

sections.heading: The Group Fitness Advantage
sections.body: If you'll actually use classes 3+ times a week, Les Mills is genuinely good value — the per-class cost beats paying drop-in studio rates, and the timetable depth is unmatched by budget chains.

sections.heading: Where Les Mills Falls Short
sections.body: If you only lift weights or train at odd hours, you're overpaying. Not all clubs are 24/7, and budget chains deliver the same iron-pumping experience for half the price.

sections.heading: Who Should Choose Les Mills (and Who Shouldn't)
sections.body: Choose Les Mills if you love group fitness, want pool access, and value premium facilities. Skip it if you're a budget-focused lifter or want guaranteed 24/7 access — a budget chain will serve you better.
